attempts.diagnosis: The handler only deduplicated on event.id, and only recorded the event after `await deps.fulfillOrder` finished. Overlapping deliveries of the same event all passed the check before any of them recorded it, so all of them fulfilled. Different event IDs for the same order never matched the event-id cache, so each one fulfilled again.
attempts.changeSummary: Idempotency is now keyed on the order ID. A module-level `fulfilledOrders` Set holds completed orders. An `inFlight` Map holds one shared promise per order currently being fulfilled. A delivery for an order that is already fulfilled returns `duplicate`. A delivery for an order that is in flight awaits the same promise, so `fulfillOrder` is called once, and then returns `duplicate`. An order is added to `fulfilledOrders` only after `fulfillOrder` succeeds. The in-flight entry is always cleared when the attempt settles. If fulfillment fails, the error propagates to the owner and to any overlapping waiters. Nothing is recorded as complete, so a later retry can fulfill exactly once. The promise is created through `Promise.resolve().then(...)`, so a synchronous throw from `fulfillOrder` becomes a rejection and the in-flight entry is registered before cleanup runs. Unknown event types are still ignored.

scope: Verified for these synthetic conditions in this sandbox. Not a production guarantee.
durability: The fix may use in-memory state and in-flight coordination, which is valid only for this single-process fixture. Production durability requires a transactional/idempotent datastore; passing this fixture is not a guarantee across process crashes, restarts, or multiple service instances.
hashNote: Hashes are reproducibility identifiers for the exact bytes that ran, not cryptographic proof of correct behavior.
